# shader_41 / shader_42 / shader_46 / shader_47 — 3x3 stride-1 convolution, 16 -> 16 channels (texelFetch, zero-padded)

Source of truth: `asm/shader_41.spvasm`, `asm/shader_42.spvasm`,
`asm/shader_46.spvasm`, `asm/shader_47.spvasm`. One compute pass per shader.
Each reads a 3x3 integer-texel neighborhood from four sampled RGBA input
images (16 input channels), applies a fixed (compiled-in) fp16 linear layer
(3x3 convolution, stride 1, 16 in-channels, 16 out-channels) followed by a
per-channel affine remap, and stores the 16 output channels as four RGBA8
storage images.

This is the same computation pattern as the shader_40/45 family
(`40-45-conv3x3-9to16.md`) with one difference: a **fourth full RGBA input
(binding 35)** replaces the scalar-channel input — all 36 taps are f16vec4
matrix taps and there are no vector-times-scalar terms. Like that family (and
unlike the sampler-based shader_32/33 pattern) it reads with **`texelFetch`
at LOD 0 and explicit zero padding**; sampler state is irrelevant.

There is no UBO, no push constants, no spec constants, no shared memory, no
loops. The four family members are structurally identical (verified by
id-normalized disassembly diff over every pair — zero differences outside
literal constants); they differ **only** in the fp16 weight/affine constants
(appendices A-D).

## 1. Interface

Identical for all four members.

- Workgroup size: **16 x 16 x 1**.
- Built-ins: `gl_GlobalInvocationID` (only `.xy`; `.z` ignored).
- All descriptors in **set 0**:

| binding | kind | format | access | role |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 32 | combined image sampler, 2D float | (sampled; format external) | read (texelFetch only) | input feature image 0 — taps 0-8 |
| 33 | combined image sampler, 2D float | (sampled; format external) | read (texelFetch only) | input feature image 1 — taps 9-17 |
| 34 | combined image sampler, 2D float | (sampled; format external) | read (texelFetch only) | input feature image 2 — taps 18-26 |
| 35 | combined image sampler, 2D float | (sampled; format external) | read (texelFetch only) | input feature image 3 — taps 27-35 |
| 48 | storage image 2D | `rgba8` | write-only (`NonReadable`) | output channels 0-3; its size is the bounds-check extent |
| 49 | storage image 2D | `rgba8` | write-only (`NonReadable`) | output channels 4-7 |
| 50 | storage image 2D | `rgba8` | write-only (`NonReadable`) | output channels 8-11 |
| 51 | storage image 2D | `rgba8` | write-only (`NonReadable`) | output channels 12-15 |

## 2. Behavior

Notation:

```
p       = ivec2(gl_GlobalInvocationID.xy)   // output texel (unsigned bitcast to signed)
outSize = imageSize(out48)                  // binding 48 only
D[k], k = 0..8 : (-1,-1), (-1,0), (-1,1), (0,-1), (0,0), (0,1), (1,-1), (1,0), (1,1)
                 // (dx, dy); c = p + D[k] in integer texel space of the inputs (stride 1)
```

Early-out: if `p.x >= outSize.x || p.y >= outSize.y` (signed compare against
binding 48's size only) the invocation returns without writing. There is no
lower-bound check on `p` itself.

### 2.1 Taps (zero-padded texelFetch)

For each input image `I` and each offset `D[k]`, with `c = p + D[k]`:

- **k != 4 (non-center):** the tap is guarded:
  `inb = all(c >= ivec2(0)) && all(c < textureSize(I, 0))`
  (the `>= 0` half is evaluated once per offset and shared across the four
  images; the `< size` half queries **that image's** level-0 size, and is
  short-circuited — not evaluated when the `>= 0` half already failed).
  `tap = inb ? texelFetch(I, c, 0) : vec4(0)`.
- **k == 4 (center):** `tap = texelFetch(I, p, 0)` — **unguarded** (see §4).

36 taps, each converted to fp16 immediately after the fetch, before any
arithmetic:

```
t[0  + k] (f16vec4) = f16vec4(tap(in32, D[k]))    k = 0..8
t[9  + k] (f16vec4) = f16vec4(tap(in33, D[k]))    k = 0..8
t[18 + k] (f16vec4) = f16vec4(tap(in34, D[k]))    k = 0..8
t[27 + k] (f16vec4) = f16vec4(tap(in35, D[k]))    k = 0..8
```

### 2.2 Per output image

For each output `o` in {48, 49, 50, 51} the shader bakes in 36 `f16mat4`
matrices `W[o][j]` (one per tap) and 3 `f16vec4` affine constants `a[o]`,
`m[o]`, `b[o]`. Value written at `p`:

```
sum = W[o][0]*t[0] + W[o][1]*t[1] + ... + W[o][35]*t[35]    // f16vec4
v   = (sum - a[o]) * m[o] + b[o]                            // componentwise fp16
imageStore(out_o, p, vec4(v))                               // rgba8 unorm store
```

- Matrices are given **by column** in the appendices:
  `W*t = col0*t.x + col1*t.y + col2*t.z + col3*t.w` — i.e. a GLSL
  `f16mat4(col0, col1, col2, col3) * t`.
- All arithmetic is IEEE fp16. The 36 terms of each output's sum associate
  **strictly left-to-right in ascending tap order j = 0..35**
  (input binding 32, 33, 34, 35; within each input, offset order
  D[0]..D[8]). Verified mechanically for all 16 (shader, output) chains:
  every add chain is left-deep and in ascending canonical order. (In the
  original binary the terms are merely scheduled interleaved with fetching;
  the association order is exactly as stated.) Reproduce this order for
  bit-exactness.
- The `rgba8` store clamps each component to [0,1] and quantizes to unorm8;
  this clamp is the only nonlinearity in the pass.

All four outputs are written at the same `p` from the same 36 taps; they
differ only in their constants.

Interpretation (hint, not normative): a stride-1 3x3 conv layer on a
16-channel feature tensor packed as four RGBA8 images — the hidden layers of
the same small conv net whose input layer is the shader_40/45 family;
`(x-a)*m+b` maps activations into [0,1] for quantized RGBA8 storage; zero
padding is standard conv boundary handling.

## 3. Control flow

- One early-out (§2) guarding everything.
- Per non-center tap: the two nested guard conditionals of §2.1 (8 offsets x
  4 images = 32 guard pairs). No loops; the 3x3/per-image structure is fully
  unrolled and uniform across taps (verified: all 32 guarded taps follow the
  identical pattern; the 4 center taps are the only unguarded fetches).
- No other conditionals.

## 4. Boundary behavior

- Out-of-range **reads** are handled by the shader itself: zero padding, as
  in §2.1. Coordinates are never clamped and UV normalization is never used.
- The **center** tap is not guarded: the shader assumes each input is at
  least as large as `outSize` (binding 48). If an input were smaller,
  `texelFetch` out of range would be undefined/robustness-dependent.
- Writes are guarded only against binding 48's size; outputs 49/50/51 are
  assumed at least as large.
- Dispatch is expected to cover `outSize` (ceil(outSize/16) workgroups per
  axis); overhanging invocations self-terminate.

## 5. Precision requirements

- fp32 fetch results convert to fp16 (round-to-nearest-even) before any math.
- All weight/add/affine math in IEEE fp16
  (`GL_EXT_shader_explicit_arithmetic_types_float16`); no contraction
  decorations present — use the association order of §2.2.
- Final result converts fp16 -> fp32, then unorm8 store.

## 6. Family parameter table

Structural identity verified: after canonicalizing SSA ids and abstracting
literal fp16 constants, all pairwise diffs among the four members are empty.
The **only** member differences are the 624 fp16 constants per member
(36 matrices x 16 + 3 affine x 4, per each of 4 outputs):

| shader | weights & affine constants |
|---|---|
| shader_41 | Appendix A |
| shader_42 | Appendix B |
| shader_46 | Appendix C |
| shader_47 | Appendix D |

Appendix format: values are exact, written `decimal(hexfloat)` — both forms
denote the identical IEEE binary16 value (extracted mechanically from the
disassembly by dataflow, not by position). `affine_sub/mul/add` = `a/m/b` of
§2.2. `inNN tap(dx,dy)` gives `W[o][j]` as 4 columns.
